# Supplied by session-deps: upstream QR-Code-generator ships only a Makefile that builds its demo
# program, so this provides the static library and install rules the rest of the build expects.
# Copied into cpp/ by the PATCH_COMMAND in qrcodegencpp.cmake.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.13)
project(qrcodegencpp CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

add_library(qrcodegencpp STATIC qrcodegen.cpp)
target_include_directories(qrcodegencpp PUBLIC $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>)

include(GNUInstallDirs)
install(TARGETS qrcodegencpp ARCHIVE DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR})
# Installed flat, not into an include/qrcodegen/ subdirectory.  Debian's package does use that
# subdirectory, but its qrcodegencpp.pc adds -I.../include/qrcodegen to compensate, whereas
# session-deps exports only its top-level include/.  Flat here is what makes `#include
# <qrcodegen.hpp>` resolve under both.
install(FILES qrcodegen.hpp DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR})
